headline: Strong El Nino -- RONI +1.69 degC (JAS 2026; legacy ONI +2.16), power index 83/100 (Very High), intensifying rapidly.
episode_status: El Nino conditions present for 4 consecutive seasons of RONI at or above +0.5 degC; 1 more needed before NOAA logs this as a formal episode.

notes: 3 candidate analogs were dropped for being too dissimilar to the current trajectory.

stormfury.verdict: 3 of 3 live storms fail STORMFURY's own criteria. Every one of them fails on supercooled water, which is the criterion no hurricane has ever passed and the reason the programme ended.
reasons: TRIGGER: the seeding agent needs supercooled liquid water and hurricane eyewalls are already glaciated at seeding altitude. Nothing to freeze, so the mechanism never starts. Willoughby et al., Bull. Am. Meteorol. Soc., 1985.

MAGNITUDE: across 36 natural eyewall expansions in 12 hurricanes this season, conserving angular momentum predicted a mean 28.0% wind drop and the storms actually gave up 4.2%, overstating it 6.6-fold. A hurricane is fed high-momentum air continuously, so a closed-system argument is an upper bound, not a forecast. STORMFURY's predicted effect came from that same calculation.

DETECTION: 20 of 282 unseeded hurricane intervals this season weakened by at least the 31% STORMFURY claimed for Debbie, and 51 moved that far in one direction or the other. An effect that size is indistinguishable from what hurricanes do untouched, which is what closed the programme.

programme.agencies: US Weather Bureau / NOAA with the US Navy

seeded_storms.name: Esther
seeded_storms.outcome: Flown before STORMFURY formally existed, as the proof of concept that got the programme funded.

seeded_storms.name: Beulah
seeded_storms.claimed: eyewall dissipated and reformed further out
seeded_storms.outcome: The first run missed the target area entirely. The second produced the reformation the hypothesis predicted, which is also what an unseeded eyewall replacement looks like.

seeded_storms.name: Debbie
seeded_storms.outcome: The showcase: five seedings on each of two days. These are the numbers the programme is remembered for, and the ones the natural replacement cycle later explained without any silver iodide.

seeded_storms.name: Ginger
seeded_storms.outcome: A large, diffuse storm with no coherent eyewall to move. It was seeded because it was what was available, which is itself a statement about how rarely the criteria above are met.

criteria.name: Supercooled water to seed

Warm-rain coalescence removes liquid water below the freezing level efficiently enough that little survives to be supercooled, leaving the seeding agent with nearly nothing to act on. The trigger is absent. The mechanism cannot start.

atlas.method: Past El Ninos (RONI >= +1.0) minus neutral years (|RONI| < 0.5), per season, per grid cell, since 1979, with each event and each neutral year counted once. Welch's t accompanies every difference and is judged against each season's own 95% point of Student's t. An event under way when the grids were built is left out.

cpc_discussion.synopsis: El Nino continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Nino likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance).
cpc_discussion.body:
El Nino strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Nino indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Nino-3.4, +3.0°C in Nino-3, and +3.9°C in Nino-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Nino.

The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Nino will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . Chances remain high for a historic event that would exceed the strength of previous El Nino events dating back to 1950 (+2.5°C or more for a 3-month RONI value ): the chance is 54% for September-November, 83% for October-December, and 70% for November-January. With an event of this magnitude, the chances of experiencing impacts consistent with El Nino are larger, though not guaranteed (see CPC outlooks for probabilities of seasonal anomalies). In summary, El Nino continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Nino likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance).
